word_order: other (main clauses show V2 word order while subordinate clauses are verb-final/SOV — e.g. main: "Die ... erklärte ..."; subordinate: "dass ... eine Republik werden sollte").
register: formal, edited informational prose (encyclopedic / news / reference-style text).
clause_boundary_signals: relative pronouns: die, der, das, welcher/welche/welches
non_boundary_traps: die / der / das (definite article vs. relative pronoun ambiguity)
in / auf / mit (prepositions that begin PPs, not clauses)
unstable_prefix_signals: die / der / das (may start a relative clause but equally often are articles)
als (could be subordinator or comparative particle)
und (coordination may continue a phrase or start a new clause)
auch (may be internal modifier or clause-opening link)
notes_for_prompt_writer: Prefer to wait for clear subordinators or the clause-final verb cluster before emitting a subordinate clause (German subordinate clauses are verb-final). In main clauses the finite verb often appears in second position — an early verb can indicate the clause head and permit an earlier split. Be cautious splitting after ambiguous tokens like die/der/das, während, als or und: they frequently occur both inside noun phrases and at clause starts and therefore can overturn an early segmentation decision.
